close_reason: On reflection: returning null for header: properties when backend omits email.headers is RFC-conformant per RFC 8621 §4.1.3 (null when header absent). Not a correctness bug.
description: email.rs handle_email_get() lines 449-464: filter_properties() is called on the full serialized email before header: values are extracted. The filtered object 'obj' has the 'headers' array only if 'headers' is in effective_props. For the header-injection path (need_headers_injected=true), 'headers' is added to the effective_props set so it survives filter_properties. However, extract_header_values() is then called on 'val' (the pre-filter full email) not on 'obj'. This is intentional and correct. BUT: if the backend does not serialize a 'headers' field on the email object, extract_header_values() will always return null/[] for every header: request regardless of actual header content, with no error. This is a silent correctness failure — not a crash, but the client gets no data back for header: properties. The backend contract for 'headers' is not documented on MailBackend.
title: Email/get: filter_properties called before header: injection — 'headers' key silently dropped if not in effective_props
